title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 87
paragraphs: This is the report given by both the Argives and the Aeginetans, and it is admitted by the Athenians too that only one man of them survived and came back to Attica. Only, the Argives say this one man survived destruction wrought by them upon the army of Athens, while the Athenians say that the divine power was the destroyer. Even this one man, however, did not remain alive but perished, they say, in the following way. When he returned to Athens he reported the disaster that had happened; and the wives of the men who had gone on the expedition to Aegina, hearing it and being very indignant that he alone of all had survived, crowded around this man and proceeded to stab him with the pins of their mantles, each of them asking where her husband was. So he was killed; and to the Athenians the deed of the women seemed far more terrible even than the disaster itself. Not knowing, it is said, how to punish the women in any other way, they changed their fashion of dress to that of Ionia—for before this the Athenian women wore Dorian dress, very like that of Corinth—they changed it therefore to the linen tunic, so that they might have no use for pins.
